newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends firm but buyers absent.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends firm but buyers absent.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended firm, fanned by a rebound in Tokyo futures, but demand was weak with hardly any buying interest, traders said.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted market indicator price for November RSS 1 buyer at 309 cents ($1.23) a kg, up half cent from Tuesday. November SMR 20 buyer was unchanged at 306 cents.
Trading houses quoted midday levels, with the SMR 20 going at 304 cents a kg, SMR10 at 305, SMR 5 at 312, SMR L at 343, SMR CV at 361 and drum latex at 234 to 235 cents.

Traders said the market was void of direction and they could not recall a single enquiry from consumers. "It was dead, in one word," said a trader. "Buyers are very well-stocked or really testing the current (price) level."
Consumer demand has been rather weak in the Malaysian rubber market in the last fortnight despite daily rains which have reduced tapping activities and supply of raw materials.
The INRO five-day average rose to 238.96 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Oct 15 from 238.95 on Oct 14. The daily indicator fell to 238.03 from 238.82 previously.
